items.question: What columns does the CSV have, in what order, and what are the header labels?
items.ticket: download their requisition list (with status and fill counts) as CSV
items.chose: Writes the header "Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created" and one column per field in that order.
items.instead: Use different header labels or order, such as raw field names like id,title,status,openings,filled,createdAt, or add a computed column such as remaining openings.

items.question: What row order does the export use?
items.chose: Sorts a copy of the input by creation time ascending, then by id with plain code-unit comparison.
items.instead: Keep the caller's input order, or sort newest first.

items.question: What is the line terminator, and is there a trailing newline after the last row?
items.chose: Ends every line, including the last row and a header-only file, with CRLF.
items.instead: Join lines with \n, or with CRLF but no trailing terminator after the last row.

items.question: Does the output start with a UTF-8 BOM?
items.chose: Prepends a BOM (U+FEFF) to the output string.
items.instead: Emit no BOM and return plain CSV text.

items.question: What does an empty requisition list produce?
items.chose: Returns the BOM and the header line only.
items.instead: Return an empty string, or throw.

items.question: How are fields containing commas, quotes or line breaks escaped?
items.chose: Wraps a field in double quotes and doubles any inner quotes when it contains a comma, double quote, CR or LF.
items.instead: Quote every field, or also guard against spreadsheet formula injection by prefixing fields that start with =, +, - or @.

items.question: How is a missing or null title rendered?
items.chose: Writes an empty field when the title is null or undefined.
items.instead: Write a placeholder such as "(untitled)" or "null", or throw.

items.question: How is the creation time formatted?
items.chose: Writes the full ISO 8601 UTC string with milliseconds, via toISOString().
items.instead: Write a date-only value such as YYYY-MM-DD, or a locale or employer-timezone format.

items.question: What happens when a requisition has an unknown or empty status?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the requisition id, and only accepts open, on_hold, filled and cancelled.
items.instead: Pass the status string through unchanged, or skip the row.

items.question: Are invalid counts (negative, fractional, NaN) for openings or filled rejected?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the id unless the value is an integer of 0 or more, so zero openings is accepted.
items.instead: Write the numbers as given, clamp them, or require openings of at least 1.

items.question: What happens when filled is greater than openings?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the id, and allows filled equal to openings.
items.instead: Export the row as is, or clamp filled to openings.

items.question: What happens with an invalid creation date, and does one bad row abort the whole export?
items.chose: Validates every row before building any output, and throws on the first invalid row (including an invalid date), so no partial CSV is returned.
items.instead: Skip or blank the bad row and export the rest, or write an empty date field.
